files.README.md:
# Payment adapter migration
The existing integration uses the provider's v1 create_charge endpoint with integer cents.
The requested change uses v2 create_payment with amount_minor, currency and a tenant-scoped
idempotency key. Old and new application versions will overlap for one deployment window.
A provider timeout can occur after the provider commits a charge. An application rollback
cannot cancel an already committed charge. The supplied local model predates this migration.
Only local artifacts are included; current provider execution and hosting settings are absent.
files.requirements.md:
# Payment requirements revision 3
Approved 2026-10-10 by payments owner.
REQ-AMOUNT: For USD, preserve the integer amount in minor units; reject unsupported currencies.
REQ-ID: For one tenant and key, identical payloads return one durable charge ID for 24 hours.
A different tenant has an independent key namespace. Conflicting payloads are rejected.
REQ-RETRY: Timeout after commit and process restart must not cause a second charge.
REQ-MIGRATE: The v1/v2 overlap must preserve the same durable idempotency identity;
customers must not be charged again when a retry reaches the other application version.
Expired keys require an explicit caller decision; do not automatically charge again.

# Checkout helper
The empty-except gate is custom gate version 1. It parses Python and rejects exception
handlers whose entire body is pass. It does not examine return values or business rules.
Other than supplied current receipts, CI history and hosting protection are unavailable.
Authorship and generation history are not recorded.

Approved by checkout owner 2026-10-10.
REQ-DISCOUNT: Preferred customers receive 15 percent off, rounded down in integer cents.
Previous revision specified 10 percent off.
REQ-ERROR: Catalog lookup failures propagate an error; they must not appear as an empty cart.

      - run: pytest --cov=checkout --cov-branch tests

files.README.md:
# Local status badge helper
This private utility is used only by an offline local developer display. Its sole assessed
behavior is is_terminal(Status) for the four declared Status enum members. The caller supplies
a validated enum; arbitrary inputs, network behavior, persistence and deployment are outside
the interface. There is no service, third-party adapter or package release in this repository.
Supported environments are CPython 3.12.6 on Linux and macOS. The module has no external dependencies.
Current immutable check receipts and a repository-settings export are included for this snapshot.
A long-term review/incident portfolio maintenance process has not yet been established.
files.requirements.md:
# REQ-TERMINAL revision 4
Approved 2026-10-10 by the developer-display domain owner, Mira.
The Status enum has QUEUED, RUNNING, DONE and CANCELLED. is_terminal returns False for
QUEUED and RUNNING, and True for DONE and CANCELLED. This is the complete input domain.
The expected table was authored by the domain owner before the current implementation.
No behavior for arbitrary strings, foreign objects or dynamically modified enum classes is promised.
files..github/workflows/verify.yml:
name: verify-enum
on: [pull_request, workflow_dispatch]
jobs:
  truth-table:
    strategy:
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12.6'
      - run: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
